declared_failures: Spec 5.6 — ambient occlusion in the junctions (wall/road, wall/house, car/ground) is NOT implemented: there is no SSAO and no baked AO; only the texture AO channel and the projected contact shadow under each car. Visible in S5/S9/S11.

Spec 5.6 — lens flare is NOT implemented; the sun is a clamped HDRI disc plus bloom, so the sun disc is not crisply visible in S1 (the sun-facing shots burn out in the glare). S4 and S8 were framed with the sun outside the picture: that is a composition choice, not a fix.

Spec 5.1 — the two cars are continuous curved procedural bodies (> 15 k triangles, 10–11 materials) but their design is stylised and far from the commercial references: bulbous nose, no mirrors/handles/vents/wing struts, tyres without sidewall detail.
Spec 4 (Z4) — 'Bosque' is a pine-and-olive slope with a bridge, not a dense forest; S6 does not read as woodland the way refs 08/10 do.
Spec 4 (Z1) — rocks standing in the water are few and small in frame (S3): 4 boulder variants with an animated white-water ring each; the beach has no dune vegetation tufts or puddles in that view.
Spec 5.6 — motion blur is a speed-driven radial blur (car and HUD excluded), much weaker than refs 01/06/13; there is no depth of field.
Spec 13.3 — the Low preset was not run on an integrated GPU; only this desktop was measured.

gates.P1: Terrain outside the corridor is a generated height-field: slopes are smooth, there are no hand-modelled cliff faces, and the ravine under the viaduct is a plain eroded slope (S7).
gates.P2: The car bodies are procedural (swept cross-sections + analytic lamp / grille / panel-gap shader). Continuous curved surfaces, but proportions are stylised; clearcoat reflections come from a 2048×1024 environment so they are softer than a real probe. S2 does not match ref 11 in detail, wing, vents or light.
gates.P3: Z1 has sea with waves, foam, wet sand and rocks with white-water rings, but no AO at wall/road junctions, no lens flare and only a mild radial motion blur. The rocks are four displaced-icosahedron variants.
gates.P4: Vegetation is alpha-card foliage with 5 species and a few variants each. The viaduct is a deck + piers + abutments (no arches, no tunnel). The village has 80 houses near the road and a church whose spire is visible in S5 but small.
gates.P5: The test autopilot is the same driver code as the AIs; scripted skid / wall-contact manoeuvres are used only inside the audio lap to provoke those sounds. All 13.1 / 13.2 checks pass in this run.
gates.P6: Performance was measured on one desktop GPU (RTX 3070 Ti) with the frame-rate limiter off; the Low preset was never run on an integrated GPU.

differences: Ref 01 streaks the road and the roadside with strong anamorphic motion blur and a dusty bloom that lifts the shadows; ours is almost sharp at 103 km/h (only a faint radial blur at the frame edges, with the car and HUD masked), so the speed feeling is much weaker.

Ref 01 silhouettes tall dark palms against a blown-out sunset with warm rim light; ours has small, front-lit mid-green palms and umbrella pines, and the sun is only a bright patch behind the start gantry (no visible disc, no god-rays).

Ref 01's hero car has reflective paint, decals, a big wing and detailed tail lamps; ours is a rounded orange GT seen from behind with a plain paint, a small wing and no decals, mirrors or exhaust detail.
Ref 01/02 have dense dust, scrub and pebbles beside the road; the right side of ours is a smooth dune slope with sparse grass tufts and a stone wall, and the left shows only a sliver of sea.
s1.veto: No car under the ground or floating; the road is textured (cracks, rubber line, worn edge) not a flat grey band; sea and sky are present (sky 23 %); shadows of poles and walls are clearly visible; no solid-colour area; no pop-in seen; the sun-side of the frame (top-left) is burnt out by glare and the sun disc itself is not visible; the dune slope on the right is the emptiest stretch ('trecho vazio' is borderline) and the palms/pines repeat a few variants.
s1.below_target: speed feeling (blur), sun disc and rays, roadside density, car detail.

differences: Ref 11 is a wide-body Supra with a carbon wing on struts, side vents, LED tail lamps and a plate; ours is a smooth bubble GT: no wing struts, vents or mirrors in view, one continuous orange paint with a mesh grille and a chrome frame as the only front detail.
Ref 11 sits in a ruined hangar with volumetric rays, dust and hard sun/shadow contrast; ours stands on an open street with soft sunset light, no volumetrics and a plain grid-box marking.
Ref 11's wheels are deep-dish with big calipers and low-profile tyres with sidewall branding; ours has 10-spoke rims, discs and calipers but round, thick tyres with no sidewall text.
Ref 11's surroundings are rich (tyre stack, vines, rust, a second car in shadow); ours has a repeated line of palms/pines and a second car of the same design in the background.
s2.veto: Not a car of boxes (curved body, rounded arches), glass is tinted with sky reflection and an interior (not flat black), the contact shadow is present, no floating/sunken wheels, shadows are visible; the weakness is the stylised proportions, not a veto item.
s2.below_target: car design, reflections resolution, background richness; no HUD by design.

differences: Ref 04 has dune fences, rippled sand, wet reflective patches and tufts of dune grass; ours is a pebbly wet-sand texture with a smooth foam band and no vegetation, puddles or fence in this frame (the 98 sand-fence pieces are elsewhere on the beach).
Ref 02 has big detailed rock faces and pebbles; ours has only four small boulders standing 15–25 m out in the surf, each with a faint white ring, so the 'rochas com espuma' read weakly.
Ref 02's sea is turquoise in the shallows with a bay and mountains; ours is pale foam into flat blue with little depth colour change in view and only a haze-grey hill on the horizon.
Ref 02/04 contain cars and dust; the AIs and the player are off-frame in ours (placed behind the camera line), so no cars are visible here.
s3.veto: Sea is not flat or foam-less (animated shore foam and rings around rocks), wet sand is darker, the sky is large (48 %), shadows are minimal because the frame is mostly sand/sea; no solid-colour area but the sand texture repeats across the lower half of the frame (texture repetition borderline).
s3.below_target: rock size/number in frame, beach life (fences, tufts), no cars in the frame, sea colour depth.

differences: Ref 02 shows a tall stratified rock face on the left and a sweeping beach below; ours looks down from a stone terrace onto a smooth orange-beige slope: the cliff has no rock strata, only terrain texture.
Ref 02 scatters cacti, shrubs and boulders; ours is dominated by one large olive tree in the left third of the frame, with a few shrubs, chevron signs and a wooden fence.
Ref 02's sea is a curved bay with surf and mountains; ours is a straight, calm horizon under a warm haze with no coastline shape and no surf visible from this height.

The ref's hero truck fills the frame and throws dust; our cars are small on the serpentine below (kerb, chevrons and guard-rail are readable, the white hatch is the only car in frame and raises no dust).
s4.veto: Road has kerb stripes, chevrons and a guard-rail (not a grey band); the sea and a large sky (31 %) are visible; nothing floats; the sun was deliberately kept out of the frame so there is no burnt-out area; the stone terrace in the foreground repeats one tile.
s4.below_target: cliff geometry, vegetation variety, coastline shape, car scale/dust.

differences: Ref 05 puts a large adobe church with a bell gable, people and vehicles on a plaza; ours shows the church only as a small red-roofed spire between the houses ahead, with no plaza activity or people.

Ref 06 has stone cottages with chimneys, climbing plants and overhanging trees under strong motion blur; ours has plaster houses with shutters, balconies and flower boxes but clean facades, no climbing plants and few street trees.
Ref 07 shows grimy plaster up close; ours uses 1k plaster tiles that look clean in the shade and have no ambient occlusion where wall meets pavement.
The player's car sits small at the bottom of the frame and the asphalt takes about a third of the image (cracks vary it, but it is a large repeated surface).
s5.veto: Houses have roofs with eaves, windows with recess and shutters, doors and balconies (not cubes); the street is open sky (sky 39 %); no objects through the road; texture repetition on the asphalt is acceptable but visible; no pop-in seen.
s5.below_target: landmark prominence, facade grime/vegetation, AO, people/activity.

differences: Ref 10 has dense tall pines with volumetric rays, dust and orange leaf litter; ours is a wide-spaced line of umbrella pines on a dune slope under a bright sky, with no rays or dust, so it does not read as a forest.
Ref 08 has lush undergrowth (ferns, broad leaves) and haze depth; ours has sparse grass tufts and shrubs on dry orange-brown ground.
Ref 08's road is a dusty dirt track with tyre marks and dust clouds behind the cars; ours is clean asphalt with no dust from the cars.
Ref 10's low sun comes through the trunks and rim-lights the leaves; ours has side light and long shadows on the road but the canopy is not translucent.
s6.veto: Not an enclosed corridor (sky 28 %), tree variants are visible but not identical in line, shadows are visible; the density of trees is the weakness.
s6.below_target: forest density, undergrowth, dust, translucent foliage.

differences: Ref 14 is a large concrete overpass over a rocky desert valley with cliff outcrops; ours is a five-pier deck viaduct over a bare, smoothly eroded ravine with no rock outcrops.

The deck-to-terrain joint in ours is a stone abutment wall at the left plus the slope; the terrain texture repeats a dotted orange pattern on the ravine floor, unlike the varied rock and gravel of the ref.
Ref 14 shows vehicles on the structure and on the road below; ours has the cars before the entrance (off-frame) and no traffic under the bridge.
Ref 14 has railings, joints and cable/lamp details on the deck; ours has a plain parapet with lamp posts and a flat concrete underside.
s7.veto: The bridge is anchored to the terrain (abutments and piers go below ground), nothing floats, sky is large (35 %); the ravine floor is a plain slope and the only repeated pattern is the ground texture.
s7.below_target: structure detail (no arches), terrain richness, traffic.

differences: Ref 13 shows three distinct cars at close three-quarter-front range under heavy motion blur; ours shows four sharp cars from behind on a bend, with only a faint blur at the frame edges, so only tail lamps and wings are visible.
Ref 09/13 cars are different makes with real grilles, lights, mirrors and decals; ours repeat the two procedural designs (blue GT, orange and red hatch/GT) with plain paint and no mirrors or decals.
Ref 09 sprays dust and leaves around the pack; ours has almost no particles in this frame (light tyre smoke only when sliding).
The ref's pack sits in rich surroundings (autumn trees, houses); ours shows the sea front with a wall, a lamp post and a few palms, and the asphalt fills the lower half of the frame.
s8.veto: Cars are side by side on the road with contact shadows and visible side light; nothing floats or clips; the sky is open (31 %); no burnt-out area in this framing (the sun is outside the frame).
s8.below_target: car variety and detail, motion blur, dust, background richness.

differences: Against a commercial close-up (e.g. refs 02/04 road edges) ours has a clean red/white kerb, a cracked asphalt tile and a guard-rail, but no tyre marks, debris, sand drift or gravel on the kerb.
The stone wall beside the kerb repeats the same 1k stone tile and has no moss, stains or AO at its base.
Guard-rail is a swept metal profile with posts and reflectors but no bolts, overlaps or dents.
The distant car is small and the foreground has no car, so there is no sense of speed.
s9.veto: Asphalt is textured with paint lines and a worn edge (not a flat band); kerb and guard-rail are present; no solid-colour area.
s9.below_target: surface wear details, AO, foreground subject.

differences: Same camera and cars as S5 in the Low preset: internal resolution is 0.75×, so edges (power poles, balcony rails, roof tiles) are softer than in S5.
No MSAA in Low: roof edges and window frames show more stair-stepping than S5.
Shadows use 2 cascades at 1024 px, so shadow edges on the facades are blockier and the far shadows fade earlier; motion blur and AO are off (the latter is off in both).
Textures, house forms and road detail are unchanged — Low does not turn into flat blocks.
s10.veto: Same assessment as S5: not blocks, open sky, textured surfaces.
s10.below_target: not tested on an integrated GPU.

differences: In a commercial scale shot the wall base would have AO, stains and plants; ours has clean plaster down to the pavement with no contact darkening.
The house door (2.1 m) and the three storeys (~3 m each) are readable against the 4.55 m car, but the car has no mirrors or door handles visible from the side, unlike the refs' cars.
The windows are recessed with shutters but have no curtains, glass reflection variety or interior.
The car's tyres are not squashed by load and the wheel arches are generous, so the car looks lighter than a real coupé next to a real wall.
s11.veto: Car and house are plausible in scale, with shadows; the street wall behind the car is the same stone tile as elsewhere.
s11.below_target: AO, wall grime, car side detail.

differences: From above the terrain texture shows a dotted/tiled pattern and blotchy dirt patches that a commercial map would hide with macro variation.
The white rings around the sea rocks look like bubbles from this height.
The track is a thin ribbon without start-line, sector or zone markers; the HUD is hidden by design.
Houses are tiny red/white specks and the forest is scattered green dots; no landmarks are labelled.
s12.veto: The whole lap is visible in one frame (Orla at the bottom, serpentine on the left, village top, bridge top right).
s12.below_target: map readability and terrain macro variation.

limitations: Single machine: every number in this report comes from one desktop (RTX 3070 Ti, Ryzen 7 5700G, headless Chrome). The ≥ 60 FPS target for an integrated GPU in the Low preset is unverified.
The cars are procedural and stylised; they are not at the level of the commercial references (nose shape, arch edges, mirror/handle details, interior).
No screen-space ambient occlusion, no lens flare; motion blur is a radial blur driven by speed with the player's car and the HUD excluded. Contact shadows under the cars are projected blobs.
The circuit has a bridge, not a tunnel; the bridge changes the rolling sound and opens a reverb send.
The AIs are slower than the test autopilot (Normal difficulty ≈ 113–117 s laps vs ≈ 103 s) and there is no rubber-banding; Hard uses the same limits as the autopilot.

Music is two CC0 tracks (menu/garage/setup and results); nothing plays during the race. The engine loops come from two CC0 recordings, so the two timbres share raw material (pitched / filtered differently).
Shadow shimmer, pop-in of vegetation LODs and the 'bloom estourado' veto are judged by eye on the screenshots and video; there is no automatic detector for them.
The quality switch reloads the page (it re-creates the renderer, shadow maps and post chain), it does not hot-swap presets.

Measured FPS depends on the machine: the verifier turns the browser frame-rate limiter off for the performance step, other steps run at the display cadence (≈ 100 Hz here), so the FPS in screenshot file names is capped by it.
